νάβλα.definition: a musical instrument of ten or (acc. to; dub. sens. in acc. OGI175.9

νάγμα.definition: anything piled up, as a stone wall, J.BJ1.21.7

ναθμός.definition: upright threads in a loom, Id

ναῖρον.definition: a plant used in perfumery; prob. f.l. for in Thphr.HP9.7.3

νάκη.definition: woolly or hairy skin, Od.14.530; also of sheep, Lyc.1310; Paus.4.11.3

ναμασιπήξ.definition: crystallized by evaporation from water, Aglaïas22

ναός.definition: Dor., Thess., etc. form, Leg.Gort.1.42; inmost part of a temple, shrine containing the image of the god, Hdt.1.183, 6.19, X.Ap.15, UPZl.c.; PGnom.79

ναοφύλαξ.definition: keeper, warden of a; master or pilot of a ship, S.Fr.143

νάρδος.definition: spikenard, Nardostachys Jatamansi; Celtic nard, Valeriana celtica, Dsc.1.8, cf. Plin.HN14.107

νάρθηξ.definition: giant fennel, Ferula communis; casket for unguents, etc., Luc.Ind.29; of Aristotle's recension of Homer, carried by Alexander in a Str.13.1.27, Plu.Alex.8

ναῦς.definition: ship, Hom., etc. ; or at the ships, i.e. in the camp formed by the ships drawn up on shore, Il.2.688, 11.659; ships of war, built long and taper for speed, Th.1.41, etc.; opp. round-built merchant-ships, Hdt.1.163, et…

ναύστολος.definition: dispatched or equipped as a ship, crossing the water, A.Th.858

νεῖκος.definition: quarrel, strife, feud; strife of words, railing, abuse, Il.23.483; 7.95; Hdt.9.55

νεκάς.definition: simply, = in pl., ranks, Call.Fr.231; in pl., the dead, AP15.40.43 , cf. EM600.9

νέκταρ.definition: nectar, the specific nourishment of; later, of wine, Call.Fr.115, Nic.Al.44, Eudem.Med. ap. Gal.14.185

νέκυια.definition: a magical rite by which ghosts were; funeral ceremony, Luc.Nigr.30

νέκυς.definition: in pl., spirits of the dead, freq. in Od.11, less freq. in Il.; Od.11.29, cf.Il.15.251; Sapph.68

νέοικος.definition: newly housed, a new denizen, Epich.12; newly built, Pi.O.5.8

νεότης.definition: youthful spirit, impetuosity, Hdt.7.13: in bad sense, youthful folly, insolence, Pl.Ap.26e; And.2.7

νεῦρον.definition: sinew, tendon, once in Hom., in pl., of the; vein, Hp.Liqu.2, cf. Ruf.Onom.208

νεῦσις.definition: inclination, tendency of; title of work by Apollonius of Perga, problems where a straight line has to be drawn through a point so as to intercept a given length between two lines or curves, Papp.670.4

νέωμα.definition: fallow land just broken up, LXXJe.4.3

νηάς.definition: a gigantic animal, whose fossil remains were found in Samos, Euph. ap. Ael.NA17.28: prov., ibid

νηδύς.definition: any of the cavities in the body, Hp.de; bowels, A.Ch.757, Hp.Aër.19, etc.; Hdt.2.87; as the seat of thirst, E.Cyc.574; Id.Supp.207

νηΐτης.definition: of or belonging to a ship, consisting of ships, a fleet, Th.2.24, 4.85; A.R.4.239, etc

νηλής.definition: Ep. neut. Ep. also; Pass., unpitied, . . S.Ant.1197; . . Id.OT180

νημηθής.definition: thoughtless, Ramsay Studies in the Eastern Rom.Prov.p.123

νηνία.definition: public eulogy on great men, sometimes accompanied by the flute: hence, lament, dirge, only in Lat. nenia, a Gr. word acc. to Cic.Legg.2.24.62; cf. sq

νηνίατον.definition: a Phrygian tune for the flute, Hippon.129

νήπιος.definition: less freq. of animals, Il.2.311, 11.113; alone, the young of an animal, 17.134

νήποινος.definition: unavenged, without; like without share of, unblest with fruitful trees, Pi.P.9.58

νηρείτης.definition: or name for several kinds of sea-snails, Arist.HA530a12, 535a19, 547b23, PA679b20

νήριον.definition: oleander, Nerium Oleander, = Dsc.4.81, dub. in CIG3641b20

νίμμα.definition: water for washing; cosmetics, Crito ap. Gal.12.448; but washing of the face, Orib.Fr.82

νίννη.definition: perh. grandmother or mother-in-law, Demitsas No.416 ; also ib.No.415 ; cf

νίωπον.definition: = oil of bitter almonds, Hp. ap. Erot

νομός.definition: place of pasturage, Il.2.475; herbage, pasture, h.Merc.198: generally, food, Hes.Op.526; . . Ar.Av.1287, cf. 239

νόμος.definition: that which is in habitual practice; usage, custom, Hes.Th.66; Id.Fr.221; c. inf., where it is the custom . . , Alc.Supp.25.5; custom is lord of all, Pi.Fr.169.1; Hdt.7.104, Pl.Lg.715d; Id.Prt.337d; Hp.Art.18; Id.Mochl…

νότος.definition: south wind (opp. Arist.Mete.363b15; N. personified as god of the South wind, Hes.Th.380, 870

νοῦμμος.definition: Western Dor. = current coin, esp. of; = the silver equivalent of the bronze pound, ib.589

νύξ.definition: night: either generally, night-season; freq. with Preps., by night, Il.14.80; all night through, Paus.1.32.4; Od.19.66, etc. ; towards night, X.Cyn.11.4, HG4.6.7; , opp. Leg.Gort.2.14, SIG527.40 ; Ar.Fr.561 ; to wards…

νύσσα.definition: in a race-course; = turning-post, Il.23.332, 344; of the near horse, ib.338, cf. Theoc.24.119: metaph., turning-point of the recurrent nerve, Gal.UP16.4

ναεύω.definition: take sanctuary in a temple, Leg.Gort.1.39

ναιετάω.definition: c.acc. loci, dwell in, inhabit, etc., Il.2.841, Od.9.21, etc.; Hes.Th.816

ναίω.definition: poet. Verb, Act. only in pres. and impf; of persons, dwell, abide, mostly folld. by a Prep. of Place, etc., Il.l.c., etc.; 16.719; S.OT1105 ; Il.2.130; Hes.Th.130; Il.2.522; 6.396: c. dat. loci, 2.412, Hes.Op.18, etc.…

ναοπόλος.definition: Ion. dwelling or busied in a; as Subst., overseer of a temple, Hes.Th.991

ναρθηκίζω.definition: splint a broken limb (orig. with pieces of; splint planks together with laths, in Pass., Apollod.Poliorc.159.4

ναρθήκιον.definition: small splint, Antyll. ap; small rod used in I, Gal.10.998

ναρκάω.definition: fut. LXXDa.11.6:—grow stiff or numb, Il.8.328; Pl.Men.80b; Democr.290; Epicur.Sent.Vat.11; LXXGe.32.32; J.AJ8.8.5; of the numbness caused by the fish Arist.HA620b19, cf. Pl.Men.84b; Theoc.27.51

νάρκη.definition: numbness, deadness, caused by palsy, frost; torpedo, electric ray, which benumbs any one who touches it, Antiph.132.2, Anaxandr.41.52, etc.; Pl.Men.80a, cf. Arist.HA620b19; the Egyptian electric eel, Malapterurus elec…

νάσσω.definition: Att. fut. Hsch.: aor. (v; stuff quite full, Epict.Fr.23:— Pass., was crammed with . . , J.BJ1.17.6

ναυαρχία.definition: command of a fleet, Th.8.20,33; period of; naval supremacy, ib.1274a12

ναυκληρία.definition: life and calling of a ship-; adventure, enterprise, Id.Med.527

ναυλοχέω.definition: lie in a harbour or creek, esp. lie in wait; c.acc., lie in wait for, Th.7.4

ναυμαχέω.definition: fight by sea, Hdt.7.143, al.; with; metaph., do battle with, Ar.V.479

ναυπηγέω.definition: to be a shipbuilder, build ships, Ar.Pl.513; metaph. in Med., contrive, 'engineer', J.AJ19.2.4

ναυσίωσις.definition: = vomiting: hence gushing of blood from the veins, Hp.Fract.11

ναυστολόγος.definition: = navis dispositor, Gloss.: also, in pl., pilotage dues, ib

ναύτης.definition: seaman, sailor, Il.19.375; passenger by sea, S.Ph.901: metaph., mates in the drinking bout, Dionys.Eleg.5

ναυτιλέῳ.definition: dat. sg., perh. Coan form of The Sailor, as place-name, SIG1000.11

ναυτίλλομαι.definition: only pres. and impf. (exc. aor. subj; of the nautilus, Arist.HA622b9

ναυφύλαξ.definition: one who keeps watch on board ship

νάω.definition: only pres. and impf., Att. contr. S.Fr.5, part. Phot.:—flow, Od.6.292; Il.21.197; Epigr. ap. Pl.Phdr.264d; S.l.c.; was running with . . , A.R.1.1146; Call.Dian.224:—Pass., to be watered, Nic.Fr. 74.58. in Hom. and pre…

νεάζω.definition: impf. Agath.5.15: aor. 1 inf; to be the younger of two, S.OC374

νεάσιμος.definition: to be ploughed up, of fallow land, Gloss

νεβρίζω.definition: wear a fawnskin at the feast of Dionysus, or, as trans., robe in fawnskins , D.18.259

νεβρίτης.definition: like a fawnskin, a precious stone, Orph.L.748:—also Plin.HN37.175

νεήλατος.definition: newly-forged, Id; freshly rolled out: new cakes, D.18.260

νεικεστήρ.definition: wrangler: c. gen., one who wrangles with, Hes.Op.716

νεικέω.definition: fut. Il.10.115: aor. Ep; trans., chide, rail at, upbraid, c. acc. pers., Il.1.521, al.; 2.224; 3.38, 21.480, Od.22.225, etc.; . . , [Paris] insulted the goddesses , but praised the other , Il.24.29.—Ep. Verb, used twi…

νειοποιέω.definition: take a green crop off a field, by which it is freshened and prepared for corn, X.Oec.11.16

νείφω.definition: fut. Epic. ap. Plu.2.949b: aor; impers., it snows, Ar.Ach.1141, cf. V.773; let it snow with barley-meal, Nicopho13

νεκρόω.definition: make dead, mortify; metaph., mortify, Ep.Col.3.5

νέκρωμα.definition: lifeless, inorganic body, Simp.in de An.318.9

νεμέθω.definition: Ep. for Nic.Th.430:—in Med., once in Hom., of doves, were feeding, Il.11.635, cf. AP14.4, Keil-Premerstein Erster Bericht p.9

νεμεσάω.definition: used by Hom. and Hes. in contr. forms; grudge, J.BJ1.22.1:—Pass., ib.6.1.6

νεμεσίζομαι.definition: Ep. Verb, only pres. and impf., feel; stand in awe of, Od.1.263

νέμησις.definition: land in occupation, area, territory, IG12.894, cf.462; spreading, Aret.CA1.9

νέμω.definition: pay out, distribute a bandage, in Act. and Pass., Hp.Off.8,22, Fract.4,16, Sor.Fasc.4, al

νεόγαμος.definition: newly married, of husband or wife; married early, Ptol.Tetr.183

νεοδμής.definition: = sq., newly tamed, h.Ap.231; a newly formed marriage, E.Med.1366

νεοκμής.definition: metaph., of troops, fresh, with unimpaired strength, Aen.Tact.16.14, 38.1

νεόκοτος.definition: new and strange, unheard of, A.Pers.257 , Th.803; for the termination cf

νεοπαγής.definition: newly fixed: lately become; newly built, J.BJ3.7.20

νεοποιέω.definition: renovate, make young again, Herm. ap

νεοπρεπής.definition: befitting the young, youthful; like a youth, extravagant, opp. Plu.TG2, cf. 2.334c

νεόφοιτος.definition: having just arrived, newcomer; Pass., newly trodden, AP7.699

νεόφρων.definition: childish in spirit, dub.l. in Panyas.12.11 : freq. as pr. n

νεόφυτος.definition: newly planted, Ar.Fr.828; metaph., new convert, neophyte, 1 Ep.Ti.3.6

νεοχμόω.definition: make innovations, esp. political, mostly with; inaugurate, Arist.Mu.401a13

νεόχυτος.definition: flowing in new fashion, v.l. for in Lyr.Adesp.112

νεόψηφος.definition: calculated in a fresh way, prob. for in Suet.Ner.39

νεύρινος.definition: made of sinew, Arist.GA787b17; made or consisting of fibres, Pl.Plt.279e

νευρόω.definition: strain the sinews, nerve; in Pass., to be supplied with nerves, innervated, . . Gal.8.236; . . , . . , Id.UP9.15, 16.5

νευστάζω.definition: nod, Il.20.162; of one making signs, Od.12.194; of one fainting, 18.240, cf. 154, Theoc.25.260; BionFr.7.3; of an animal lowering its horns, Opp.C.2.467

νεύω.definition: Il.13.133, etc.: fut. Od.16.283, etc.: aor; nod, beckon, as a sign, Od.16.283; Il.9.223, cf. Od.17.330; h.Hom.7.9; Alex.91, cf. 178.3; beckon with the hand, Ezek.Exag.73: c. inf., beckon to one to do a thing, in token…

νέφρησις.definition: pain in the kidneys, dub. in Gloss

νέω.definition: metaph., of shoes that are too large, was floating in my shoes, as if they were boats, Ar.Eq.321; v. II. fin

νεώ.definition: Att. gen. and later acc. of

νεωκορέω.definition: to be a serve, tend, in Pass; ironically, sweep clean, clean out, plunder a temple, Pl.R.574d

νηέω.definition: Dor. older form of , heap, pile; pile, load, Il.9.358:—in Med., ... let him pile his ship with gold enough, ib.137, cf. 279. [Sts. corrupted to q.v.]

νήκεστος.definition: incurable, neut. as Adv., incurably, . . ib.283

νηκουστέω.definition: give no heed to, disobey, c. gen., Il.20.14

νηνεμέω.definition: to be still, of the bowels, dub. l. in Hp.Mul.2.113 ; of the weather, v.l. for in Str.7.3.18

νηνέω.definition: heap, v.l. in Il.23.139: also in compds

νηπενθής.definition: banishing pain and sorrow; free from sorrow: Adv. Protag.9

νηπιαχεύω.definition: to be childish, play like a child, Il.22.502:—Med., Rh.Mus.1879.195

νησίζω.definition: to be or form an island, Plb.3.42.7, 5.46.9; to be peninsular, Peripl.M.Eux.58

νήστης.definition: one who is fasting, on an empty; = staminarius, Gloss

νήχω.definition: Dor. :—swim, Od.5.375; ib.399; 7.280; Hes.Sc.317; Nic.Al.590:—mostly Med. part. Od.7.276, 14.352, Hes.Sc.211; inf. Democr.172: poet. impf. Titanomach.4 : fut. Od.5.364, Timo32: aor. Lyc.76; part. AP9.36 : the Med. for…

νίζω.definition: Epich.[273]; imper. Il.11.830; inf; wash off, . . Il.10.575; 11.830, 846; E.Sthen.l.c.:—Pass., Il.24.419:—Med., he washed the brine off his skin [with water] from the river, Od.6.224.—Commonly used of washing part of …

νικάω.definition: Ion. Democr.249, Herod.1.51, also; abs., conquer, prevail in battle, in the games, or in any contest, Il.3.439, etc.; the conqueror, ib.138, X.Smp.5.9, etc.; the conquered, Il.23.656,663; I won the first prize [at Oly…

νικηφορέω.definition: carry off as a prize, win naught but tears, E.Ba.1147

νιτρέλαιον.definition: emulsion of soda and oil, Zos.Alch.p.147B., Olymp.Alch.p.91 B

νοέω.definition: Aeol. : Ep. aor. 1 Il.8.91; perceive by the mind, apprehend, 11.599; . . Od.13.318, cf. Il.10.550, 24.337, etc.; Od.19.478; or did not take notice, Il.9.537, cf. 5.665; thou thyself art aware of it, Od.21.257; 18.228;…

νοήμων.definition: gen. thoughtful, intelligent; in one's right mind, opp. Hdt.3.34

νοθεία.definition: birth out of wedlock or by a marriage with; spuriousness, Olymp.in Mete.4.16

νόθος.definition: at Athens, child of a citizen father and an alien mother, D.23.213, etc.; Plu.Them.1

νομαδία.definition: pasturage, steppe, in pl., Peripl.M.Rubr.20:— Adj. ibid

νόμαιος.definition: Ion. and later Gr. for; prescribed by law, SIG589.4 , cf. GDI5699 ; ib.5653c10

νομάς.definition: roaming about for pasture; metaph., of a prostitute, Ph.2.327

νομεύω.definition: put to graze, drive afield, in Act., of the; eat down the pastures with oxen, Lat. depascere, h.Merc.492

νομίζω.definition: of a legislator, enact, X.Lac.2.4, cf. 12.3, Cyr.8.5.3: c.acc., Id.Lac.1.7:—Pass., D.C.37.20; Id.78.22; cf. I

νομομαχέω.definition: fight with laws, coined on analogy of Lollianus ap.Philostr.VS1.23.2

νομῳδός.definition: one who chants or proclaims the law, Str.12.2.9

νομώνης.definition: Boeot. official who leases public pasture, IG7.3171.43

νοοειδής.definition: having the form of Intelligence, of intelligible character, Plot.5.1.3, 5.3.8, Procl.in Ti.1.247,407 D

νοοπλανής.definition: wandering in mind, deranged, ib.4.197; Act., distracting the mind, ib.29.69

νοόω.definition: convert into pure Intelligence, in Pass., Plot.6.7.35, cf. 6.8.5; Procl.in Prm.p.491 S.; Dam.Pr.100

νοσάζω.definition: to be ill, Gal.15.302:—also in Med; causal, produce sickness, Gal.1.208, cf. 140

νοσήλιος.definition: of or for sickness: , food for sick persons, Opp.H.1.301

νοστέω.definition: go or come home, return; abs., return safe, Il.10.247; return, 2.253; . . Pi.N.11.26, etc

νόστος.definition: return home, Hom., esp. in Od; generally, travel, journey, to the land of the P., Od.5.344; journey after food, S.Ph.43; E.IA966, 1261

νοτέω.definition: to be wet or damp, drip, Call.Epigr.52; Eratosth.16.10; Nic.Al.24, 494

νοτία.definition: damp, moisture, spring; natural moisture of the body, Paul.Aeg.6.24

νουμήνιος.definition: Att. contr. for used at the; as Subst., perh. a kind of curlew: prov., 'birds of a feather flock together', D.L.9.114

νύγμα.definition: lesion of a opp. and , Gal.13.651, 883, cf. Steph.in Hp.2.439 D

νυγμή.definition: = sq., Plu.Ant.86; dot, in punctuation, Dosith.p.380 K

νυγμός.definition: pricking sensation, irritation, Ruf. ap; metaph., of the prickings of conscience, D.S.13.58; but also, = II, Plu.Phil.9

νυκτηγρεσία.definition: written = excubiae, Gloss.; nyctegresia, Fest. s.v. egretus

νυμφαία.definition: = yellow water-lily, Nuphar; white water-lily, Nymphaea alba, ibid

νύμφευμα.definition: marriage, espousal, in pl; in sg., the person married, 'a good match for him', Id.Tr.420

νυμφιάω.definition: to be in a frenzy, a disease of mares, Arist.HA604b10

νυμφών.definition: bridechamber, LXXTo.6.14; temple of Dionysus, Demeter, and Persephone, Paus.2.11.3

νύσσω.definition: Att. Pass., pf. Gal.10.221: aor; metaph., sting, Phld.Lib.p.64O.; Luc.Herm.71, cf. Porph.Abst.1.49

νυστάζω.definition: fut. LXXIs.5.27: aor; hang the head, APl.c. 'grow drowsy'.)

νωμάω.definition: Mosch.4.108:—Med., v.infr; of weapons, implements, etc., handle, wield, Il.5.594; 7.238; 3.218; . . Od.22.10; managed the sheet, 10.32; . . 12.218; Pi.I.1.15; drive, Id.P.4.18; Theophil.2.5:—Med., Q.S.3.439

νωμήτωρ.definition: one who distributes, Doroth. ap; one who guides, moves, etc., Nonn.D.12.20, 48.165

νωτίζω.definition: only in aor. exc. in compd. turn one's; cover the back of, E.Ph.654

νώτισμα.definition: that which covers the back, e.g. wings, Trag.Adesp.541

νωτοβατέω.definition: mount the back, sens. obsc., AP12.238; walk over the ridge of, ib.7.175

ναίχι.definition: Adv., for like for for S.OT684, Pl.Hipparch.232a, Men.Sam.81, Call.Epigr.30.5

νή.definition: Particle of strong affirmation, with acc. of the; in answering questions, X.Cyr.1.3.6, Pl.Prt.312a, etc.: in a supposed answer from antagonists, folld. by D.8.16

νῆα.definition: v. Adv. to the ship, Od.13.19; A.R.4.1768

νυκτιπλοέω.definition: navigate by night: hence, metaph., to be exact, Chrysipp. ap. Zen.5.32

ναυσίπορος.definition: traversed by ships, navigable, of a; parox. Act., passing in a ship, seafaring, E.Rh.48

ναυβατέω.definition: serve as in the cult of Isis , CIG2955

νεκροφορέω.definition: bear as a dead body to the burial: metaph., of soul bearing body, Ph.2.540, cf. 1.100

νεόκμητος.definition: newly wrought, Nic.Th.498; just slain, v.l. for E.Rh.887

νόημα.definition: Ion. Emp.110.10 (but; in Philos., thought, concept, opp. sensation, sense-presentation, Parm.8.34, etc.; Arist.Fr.87; Id.de An.430a28; discursive thinking, as the function of Herm. ap. Stob.2.8.31

νεβρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be changed into a fawn, Nonn.D.10.60

νυκτήγρετον.definition: Oriental plant, said to be luminous at night, Plin.HN21.62

νοητάρχης.definition: ruler of the world of Intelligence, Iamb.Myst.8.2

νωτοπλήξ.definition: with scourged back, = of slaves, Ar.Fr.830, Pherecr.89

νεοδίδακτος.definition: of dramas, poems, etc., newly produced, Luc.Tim.46

νηκηδής.definition: careless, f.l. in Epic. ap. Pl.Smp.197c

νεοσπάς.definition: newly torn away, fresh-plucked, S.Ant.1201, cf. Fr.502

νήδυμος.definition: = , from which it arises; in later Poets, not confined to sweet, delightful, h.Pan.16; APl.4.217; Nonn.D.48.602; ib.12.176

νοθεύω.definition: corrupt, Zeno Stoic.1.58; adulterate, Max.Tyr.37.4:— Pass., Plu.2.373b; Luc.Deor.Conc.7

νωτοκοπέω.definition: break an animal's back, slaughter it, Thd. Ex.13.13, Is.66.3

ναύτρια.definition: fem. of as if from Ar.Fr.825

νῦν.definition: Adv. now, both of the present moment, and of the present time generally, mortals of our day, Il.1.272; so in Ion. and Att., men of the present day, Hdt.1.68; Pi.O.1.105, B.5.4, cf. Arist.Metaph.1069a26; Th.1.6; ib.12;…

νύχιος.definition: of persons, doing a thing by night, Hes.Op.523 , cf.Th.991, A.Ag.588, etc. ; as in nightly sleep, S.Ph.857

νωθής.definition: sluggish, slothful, Il.11.559; of the understanding, dull, stupid, Hdt.3.53; Hp.Ep.17, cf. A.Pr.62, Pl.Plt.310e

νηγάτεος.definition: Ep. Adj. of doubtful meaning and derivation, perh. newly made, Il.2.43, 14.185; h.Ap.122; A.R.1.775

νεάω.definition: plough up, of fallow land, . . Ar.Nu.1117: metaph., Pratin.Lyr.5: abs., Eup.13, Thphr.CP3.20.7: aor. 1 subj. ib.3.20.8:—Pass., land ploughed up, after lying fallow, Hes.Op.462

νεκυαγωγή.definition: calling up of spirits, necromancy, PMag.Par.1.222

νακότιλτος.definition: with the wool plucked off, Cratin.41

νομιστί.definition: or Adv. conventionally, opp. Diog.Oen.6, cf. Gal.1.417

νεόλυτος.definition: resolved in a new fashion, Lyr.Adesp.112 = Trag.Adesp.136

νυκτάλωψ.definition: = night-blind, Gal.19.124, cf. Plin.HN8.203, Aët.7.48, etc; ubi homo neque matutino tempore videt neque vespertino, Ulp. in Dig.20.1.10.4

νεβρίς.definition: gen. E.Ba.136 , E.Ba.24, Thesp.1, E.Ba.249, ib.696:—fawnskin, esp. as the dress of Dionysus and the Bacchae, Il.cc

ναύφθορος.definition: shipwrecked, the garb of shipwrecked men, E.Hel.1382, 1539

νεουργέω.definition: invent new things, f.l. in Alciphr.3.51

νόστιμος.definition: belonging to a return (not in; of plants and fruit, yielding a high return, productive, Thphr.CP4.13.2 ; all things in abundance, Call.Cer.136; S.E.M.7.17

νηττάριον.definition: Dim. of foreg., duckling, used as a term of endearment, Ar.Pl.1011, Men.1041

νοσέω.definition: to be sick, ail; of passion, to be mad, S.Aj.635 ; ib.207 ; Id.Tr.1235; alone, opp. ib.435; Cratin.329; to have a morbid craving for fame, Plu.2.546f; Men.Mon.550

νώδυνος.definition: -, = , painless, Pi.N.8.50. II. Act., soothing pain, S.Ph.44

νυμφοκομέω.definition: adorn as a bride, APl.4.147; make ripe for marriage, Supp.Epigr.1.570.6

νυκτερινεία.definition: office of commander of the night- watch, Supp.Epigr.4.515.9

νηπύτιος.definition: Ep. Dim. of little child; as Adj., childish, Il.20.211; foolish, Orph.L.6

νεόδμητος.definition: newly tamed: metaph., of; newly killed, E.Rh.887 , Lyc.65

ναοειδής.definition: in the form of a shrine, SIG996.23

νόσανσις.definition: falling sick, opp. Arist.Ph.230a22, Plot.6.3.22 and 23; v.l. for Arist.Ph.229a26

νύξις.definition: pricking, stabbing, Aret.SA2.9, Gal.1.239; stinging, Dsc.2.81; impact, Plu.2.930f

νόσημα.definition: metaph., of passion, vice, etc., A.Pr.227; ib.685; ib.978; of love, S.Fr.149.1; Pl.Grg.480b, cf. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.103

νεῦμα.definition: nod, sign, Th.1.134; expression of will, command, A.Supp.373 ; Plb.21.38.4; approval, sanction, Philostr.Her.12a.1, cf. IG3.636; control, Chor.p.28B

νεοτερπής.definition: new and charming, Opp.H.3.352, etc.: neut. as Adv., with new delight, Id.C.2.584

νεκυοστόλος.definition: ferrying the dead over the Styx, of; bearing the dead, of a bier, AP7.634

νυχηβόρος.definition: devouring by night, v.l. for Nic.Th.446

νηοπορέω.definition: poet. for go by sea, AP7.675

νησιαρχέω.definition: to be governor of an island or group of islands, CIG3655.7

νεόπτολις.definition: poet. for new- founded city, A.Eu.687

νευροσπαδής.definition: drawn by the string, the arrow drawn and just ready to fly, S.Ph.290

νωδυνία.definition: relief from pain, Pi.P.3.6, cf. Theoc.17.63

νεκρόπολις.definition: city of the dead, a name given to a suburb of Alexandria, Str.17.1.10 and 14

νεκύδαλος.definition: or the nympha of the silkworm, Arist.HA551b12, Ath.8.352f

νεκυάμβατος.definition: of Charon's boat, embarked in by the dead, Epic. ap. Paus.10.28.2

νεαροποιέω.definition: make new, refresh, Plu.2.702c:—in Med; Medic., freshen the edges of an ulcer by removing granulations, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.4, Ruf. ap.eund.8.24.48

νεμεσίτης.definition: Nemesis-stone, a stone with magical properties, Cyran.30

ναύπλιος.definition: a kind of shell-fish, Peripl.M.Rubr.17; f.l. for Artem.2.14

νεβρισμός.definition: wearing of a Arignote ap. Harp

νέατος.definition: Ep. poet. Sup., uttermost, lowest, Hom. , always of Space, the lowest part of . . , Il.5.293,857, 15.341; extreme, outermost, Od.7.127; Il.14.466; 8.478; the lowest slope of Ida, 2.824; Sol.13.10; the feet, Orac. ap.H…

νεόρραντος.definition: newly sprinkled, a fresh-reeking sword, S.Aj.30, 828; newly shed, Aristid.Or.24 . 44

νοτόθεν.definition: Adv. from the south, Pl. ap. D.L.3.41, Thphr.Sign.11,21: c. gen., prob.l. in IG12.4.9

νεοσύστατος.definition: recently formed, i.e. recent, of; having newly joined a sect, proselyte, J.BJ2.8.9

νυμφεύτρια.definition: she who escorts the bride, bridesmaid; = Lib.Decl.26.13

ναυάγιον.definition: Ion. piece of wreckage; later, = Str.4.1.7

νήκουστος.definition: deaf, not hearing; unheard, unknown, Arat.173

νοθεῖος.definition: of or belonging to a inheritance of a Lys.Fr.140S., cf. Ar.Av.1656

νεοσίγαλος.definition: new and sparkling, with all the gloss on, metaph., Pi.O.3.4

νεωτερισμός.definition: attempt to change; esp. in bad sense; generally, change, as of diet, Sabin. ap. Gal.17.562

νεοπενθής.definition: in new sorrow, fresh-mourning; Pass., lately mourned, IG12.447.6 , cf. 14.1663

ναυσθλόω.definition: carry by sea, E.Tr.162; Pass., to be visited by ships, Lyc.1415

νυμφοπόνος.definition: busied with the bride, title of a poem by Sophron, Ath.8.362c

νεκροφόρος.definition: burying corpses, burying the dead, Plu.Cat.Ma.9, Gloss

νεώτερος.definition: Comp. of of persons, younger; Sup., Il.7.153, etc.; opp. Arist.Pol.1305a29

ναρκόω.definition: benumb, deaden, Hp.Liqu.6; ib.1: c. acc. pers., Phld.Rh.1.380 S., cf. Hp.Epid.6.2.1

νυκτερίς.definition: a fish, = Opp.H.2.205; a plant, = Aët.12.1

νέορτος.definition: newly arisen, S.OC1507; of persons, new, Id.Tr.894 ; also, youthful , S.Fr.872

νυκτολάλημα.definition: spell for making a woman talk in her sleep, PMag.Lond.121.411

νυκτερέτης.definition: one who rows or fishes by night, AP6.11

νυκτερεία.definition: hunting by night, taking game asleep, Pl.Lg.824

νεόδαρτος.definition: newly stripped off, Od.4.437; newly flayed, X.An.4.5.14

νηττοφόνος.definition: duck-killer, a kind of eagle, Aquila naevia, Arist.HA618b25

νεφεληδόν.definition: Adv. in the manner of clouds, Nonn.D.15.1

νομοθέτις.definition: fem. of coined as expl. of Corn.ND28

νυχεύω.definition: fut. Nic.Fr.74.8:—watch the night through, pass the night, E.El.181 , cf. Rh.520, Hyps.Fr.10, 11.13 ; with them, Nic.l.c

νεάτη.definition: Dor. Philol.6:—the lowest of the three strings which formed the framework of the musical scale , but the highest in pitch, Cratin.134, Pl.R.443d:— contr. Arist.Ph.224b34, Metaph.1018b28, 1057a23, Alex.Eph. ap.Theon Sm…

νουθετέω.definition: put in mind: hence, admonish, warn; metaph., chastise, Ar.V.254, Pl.Lg.879d:—Pass., coupled with Id.Grg.478e

νεκροθήκη.definition: coffin or urn, E.Fr.472.17 ; place for a coffin or urn, prob. in Rev.Bibl.39.532

ναυκρατέω.definition: have the command of the sea, Th.7.60:—Pass., to be mastered at sea, X.HG6.2.8

νεκυσσόος.definition: rousing the dead to life, Nonn.D.44.204

νήνεμος.definition: without wind, calm; metaph., E.Hec.533; Plu.2.589d

νεοσπαδής.definition: = newly drawn from a wound, bloody, A.Eu.42

νευρορράφος.definition: one who makes strings for the lyre, Lycurg.Fr.100

νομεύς.definition: dealer out, distributor, Pl.Lg.931d, cf. Min.317d, 321b

νεήτομος.definition: cut or castrated when young, AP6.234

νηπελέω.definition: to be powerless, Hp. ap. Gal.19.124: hence restored in Id.Mul.2.113; cf

νυμφότιμος.definition: honouring the bride: bridal song, A.Ag.705

νυμφαγωγέω.definition: pf. Plb.25.4.10:—lead the; of the bridegroom, lead home a bride, Charito2.1

νωταγωγέω.definition: carry on the back, Clearch. ap. Ath.6.258b

νεηγενής.definition: Ion. for new-born, just born, Od.4.336

νομαῖος.definition: = AP6.157 ; a shepherd's cry, Call.Fr.310; growing in pastures, Nic.Th.67

νεαροπρεπής.definition: possessing youthful charm, metaph., of style, Aristid.Rh.2p.551S.; becoming or natural in youth, Procl.in Alc.pp.23,47 C.; Id.in Cra.p.1 P., cf. Olymp.in Phlb.p.249S

ναυκρατής.definition: master or mistress of the sea, Hdt.5.36

νηπιέη.definition: Ep. form for childhood, childishness, Il.9.491: in pl., Od.1.297; . . in childish fashion, Il.15.363; led them in his folly, Od.24.469

νεότομος.definition: fresh-cut, A.Ch.25; freshly cut off, E.Ba.1170

νυμφοτομία.definition: removal of the clitoris, Philum. ap. Aët.16.115 tit., Paul.Aeg.6.70 tit

νικητής.definition: winner in games, CIG5035 ; conqueror, Eust.157.1; of the Emperor Julian, SIG906B

ναπαῖος.definition: of a wooded vale or dell, S.OT1026; E.HF958; a sylvan god, Ael.NA6.42, cf. 7.2

νοσφίζομαι.definition: allontanarsi, separarsi; sottrarre, privare (da νόσφι: lontano, in disparte); aor. ἐνοσφισάμην
